status.title: Status
status.subtitle: Services, queues and the latest runs.
status.pipelineIntro: Each document travels left to right. Two background queues do the work; the search index at the end is what you search.

source.title: Nextcloud
source.desc: Your watched folders. Read only — nothing is ever written back.

crawlStage.title: Crawl
crawlStage.desc: Walks the folders level by level (PROPFIND), spotting new and changed files by their ETag. Queues each one for processing.

processStage.title: Process
processStage.desc: Downloads the file, extracts text and metadata via Tika (OCR for scans), renders the preview image, and writes the document into the search index.

indexStage.title: Search index
indexStage.desc: Meilisearch. Once a document lands here it is findable.

status.runTypeHint: A full run reprocesses every file; a changes-only run touches just what changed since last time.
status.clearConfirmBody: {count} queued jobs will be discarded. Documents already in the index stay untouched — anything not yet processed is picked up again on the next run.
status.indexActionFailed: The action could not be completed.
status.rebuildConfirmBody: The index and all document records are dropped, then every folder is crawled and processed from scratch. This takes a while — search stays incomplete until it finishes.
status.clearIndexConfirmBody: Every document is removed from the index and its record. Search returns nothing until you rebuild or the folders are crawled again. This cannot be undone.

tags.autoDesc: Hangs on every document indexed for the first time. A folder's initial stock stays clear.
tags.enabledDesc: A tag switched off disappears from the filter and the picker; its assignments stay.

mcp.title: MCP access
mcp.desc: NextSearch speaks the Model Context Protocol. An assistant such as Claude can search and set tags through it — with your permissions, the same folders, the same tags.
mcp.urlHint: Add this address in the client as a custom connector.
mcp.viaOauthDesc: The client fetches its own access. You end up on an approval page here and decide what it may do. This is the way for Claude Desktop.
mcp.viaKeyDesc: For clients that cannot fetch anything themselves: create an API key and set it as a bearer token.
mcp.connectionsDesc: Whatever fetched access through the browser. A key lives in the tab next door.
mcp.revokeConfirm: “{name}” loses access immediately. For a new connection the application has to ask again.

mcp.docsHint: Setup, tools and pitfalls are in docs/mcp.md in the repository.

documents_read.label: Search and read documents

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: What this installation does, with the values that currently apply.
help.footnote: The numbers and lists on this page come from the running installation. Change a folder, a format or a tag, and it reads differently the next time you open it.

overview.title: What is in here
overview.body: NextSearch reads the folders listed below, extracts the text from the files and makes it searchable. The files themselves stay in Nextcloud; what lives here is the text, a preview image and the metadata.
overview.noFolders: No folder has been shared with you yet. The administrator of this installation can change that.
overview.noFoldersAdmin: No folder is set up yet. Connect a Nextcloud under Administration › Instances, then pick a path under Folders.
overview.changelogHint: What changed from version to version is under

search.title: Searching
search.body: The search covers the contents of the files, the file name and the folder names in the path. Case does not matter, and small typos are absorbed by the index. More words narrow the result rather than widen it.
search.figure: Result list with the filter column
search.ocrOn: PDFs without a text layer and image files go through text recognition, set to {languages}. That takes longer than a file that carries its own text.
search.ocrOff: Text recognition is switched off. Scanned PDFs without a text layer are indexed, but without their text.

filter.title: Filtering
filter.body: The column beside the results shows what occurs in the current result, with counts: {facets}. One click narrows, a second one takes the filter back off.
filter.combining: Several values of the same category act as “or” — pdf or docx. Values from different categories act as “and” — pdf from 2019. The counts follow whatever else is selected.
filter.figure: Filter column showing what occurs in the current result

documents.title: Opening documents
documents.body: A hit leads to the document page: preview of the first page, metadata, tags. From there the original can be viewed in the browser or downloaded — no Nextcloud account needed, the credentials stay on the server. Markdown, text files and e-mails are rendered by NextSearch itself.
documents.previewOff: Preview images are switched off in this installation.
documents.figure: Document page with preview and tags

tags.title: Tags
tags.body: The search finds what a file says. Tags record what it means to the people working with it, and in the filter they are a category like any other.
tags.figure: The tag picker on a document
tags.noteAutoDays: assigned automatically, falls off after {days} days
tags.empty: No tags have been created yet.
tags.own: You create your own tags straight from a document, or under User settings › My tags. They belong to you alone — nobody else sees them or where you put them.

saved.title: Saving searches
saved.body: A search including its filters and sort order can be saved below the search field and recalled with one click. Saved searches belong to you and are collected under “Saved searches”.

access.title: Your access
access.body: Password, two-factor sign-in, your own tags and your keys are under User settings.
access.twoFactorOn: Two-factor sign-in is enabled for your account.
access.twoFactorOff: Two-factor sign-in is not enabled for your account.
access.apiBody: Searching and tagging also work over HTTP, with a personal key as a bearer token. The key can do exactly what you can do. The limit is {limit} requests per minute.
access.mcpBody: An assistant such as Claude can search and set tags over the Model Context Protocol. Available tools: {tools}.
access.mcpOauth: Add the address in the client as a custom connector. The client sends you to an approval page here, where you decide what it may do.
access.mcpKeyOnly: Signing in through the browser is switched off. A client needs a personal key as a bearer token.
access.figure: Connected applications in the user settings

admin.title: Administration
admin.body: The scheduler checks every minute which folder has passed its interval. The default is {minutes} minutes per folder, adjustable per folder.
admin.people: Accounts: {users}, {admins} of them with administrator rights.
admin.states: {total} documents in the database, {failed} failed, {skipped} skipped. Skipped means the format is not covered or the file is too large.
admin.permissions: The shares here have nothing to do with the permissions in Nextcloud. Whoever is granted a folder reads its contents in full text and opens the originals — regardless of what Nextcloud itself would allow.

setup.title: Nothing to search yet
setup.subtitleAdmin: Three steps to the first hit.
setup.subtitleUser: Setup is still under way. What is missing can only be added by an administrator.

instance.title: Connect a Nextcloud
instance.body: Address, user and an app password. NextSearch only ever reads.

folder.title: Pick a folder
folder.body: Choose a path from the connected Nextcloud. Subfolders come along.

indexing.title: Let it index
indexing.body: The first run starts on its own. How long it takes to pull the text out of the files depends on how many there are — longer for scanned PDFs that go through text recognition.
indexing.bodyPending: {pending} files still to go, {indexed} done. The page pulls in new hits by itself.
